answers.answer: The summary says the standard game has 16 rounds divided into 4 seasons, each ending with a courtship round, but it does not state how many ordinary turns each player takes. It says courtship compares VP in the current theme category, the sole winner takes a Fairchild card, each winner draws 1 VP card, 1 objective is discarded, and the first-player pawn passes. Service rotation and ongoing tile benefits during courtship are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Overview: “16 rounds (standard) ... divided into 4 seasons, each ending with a courtship round.” Courtship Round: “Compare VP totals in the current theme category. Sole winner takes a Fairchild card. Each winner draws 1 VP card. Discard 1 objective card. Pass first-player pawn.”

answers.answer: The listed Standard Turn order is: refresh servants; host an activity; invite guests; provide service; enjoy favors; buy 1 improvement tile; clear the board. A theme card is revealed at the start of each season. The summary does not say when round-track events or ongoing effects resolve. At cleanup, it says to return the tile and servants and discard used guests, but does not specify their precise destinations.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Reveal a theme card at start of each season.” Standard Turn steps 1–7, including “Clear Board: Return tile and servants; discard used guests.”

answers.answer: The summary gives the passing sequence as: move all servants to Available Service, recover discarded guests to the active hand, gain £200 or a free market refresh, and a player may still buy from the Builders’ Market. It does not state where this fits relative to round events or ongoing effects. The two listed passing benefits are £200 or a free market refresh. Butler’s Room hiring as a passing benefit is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Passing Turn: “Move all servants to Available Service. Recover discarded guests to active hand. Gain £200 or free market refresh. May still buy from Builders’ Market.”

answers.answer: The summary supports that reputation must meet or exceed an activity tile’s prestige and that reputation must meet guest prestige. It does not say whether screening uses reputation after step 2 or whether the described activity remains legal after four Service Help actions lower reputation to 3.4. Which servants Service Help can refresh is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Standard Turn: “Your reputation must meet or exceed the tile’s prestige”; “Reputation must meet guest prestige.”

answers.answer: The summary does not describe the ordering of positive and negative favors, taking a negative reputation favor at minimum reputation, or the requirement for playing a guest with a money penalty. These requested parts are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Standard Turn step 5 only says: “Enjoy Favors: Gain money, reputation, new guests, VP cards, or other benefits from the activity.”

answers.answer: The listed special actions are: gain £100 for 2 reputation increments, repeatable; refresh 1 servant for 3 reputation increments, repeatable; refresh the Builders’ Market for 4 reputation increments, once per turn. A minimum-reputation restriction and whether service help can take a servant directly from Expended Service are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Special Actions: “Gain £100 at cost of 2 reputation increments (repeatable). Refresh 1 servant at cost of 3 reputation increments (repeatable). Refresh Builders’ Market at cost of 4 reputation increments (once per turn).”

answers.answer: The summary does not describe hiring through the base Butler’s Room, guest attendance at that activity, where new hires go, or how upgrading changes recruitment. Those requested parts are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Components lists servant meeples and the setup places “servants for hire”; no Butler’s Room hiring procedure is given.

answers.answer: The summary gives Housekeeper-for-Lady’s-Maid as an example of an allowed substitution. It does not state when that substitution is permitted, whether a Footman may substitute for a Valet, or whether an Underbutler may substitute while the regular male servant is available.
answers.evidence: Servant Types: “Some substitutions allowed (e.g., Housekeeper for Lady’s Maid).”

answers.answer: How an Underbutler is acquired, when it is available, and whether another player can recruit it are unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Servant Types lists “Underbutler” but gives no acquisition or availability rule.

answers.answer: The summary says a player may purchase 1 improvement tile from the Builders’ Market by paying its cost plus any modifier. It does not give the price formula in the Market or Reserve, the minimum price, or whether owned or above-reputation tiles may be bought.
answers.evidence: Standard Turn step 6: “Purchase 1 improvement tile (pay cost + any modifier).”

answers.answer: The summary does not describe Market refilling after a purchase, remaining tiles, duplicate draws, Reserve-eligible tiles, multiple new draws, or whether buying one tile from a duplicate stack causes a refill. All requested parts are unsupported.
answers.evidence: The summary says only “Purchase 1 improvement tile” and that the Builders’ Market is filled during setup; it gives no refill procedure.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, service tiles move to the Reserve; after courtship 2, prestige-1 tiles move to the Reserve. The summary does not state an exception, what happens to later draws, or whether a full seasonal Market refresh is standard.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: “After Courtship 1 | Service tiles to reserve”; “After Courtship 2 | Prestige-1 tiles to reserve.”

answers.answer: For courtship, the summary says to compare VP totals in the current theme category; the sole winner takes a Fairchild card; each winner draws 1 VP card; and 1 objective is discarded. It does not say how existing Fairchilds are returned or how ties are handled. The first-player pawn passes, but the direction is not stated.
answers.evidence: Courtship Round: “Compare VP totals in the current theme category. Sole winner takes a Fairchild card. Each winner draws 1 VP card. Discard 1 objective card. Pass first-player pawn.”

answers.answer: Final courtship scoring, tie resolution, and permitted last actions are unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: The summary describes courtship generally but does not distinguish final courtship or mention last actions.

answers.answer: The summary lists VP from improvement tiles, gentry cards, completed objectives, reputation level, servants (2 VP each), money (1 VP per £200), and retained VP cards. It does not give the point values for reputation levels 1–7 or specify wealth rounding. The stated tiebreak order is Fairchild card holder, then reputation; any further tiebreak is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions lists those categories, “2 VP per servant,” and “1 VP per £200”; Tiebreaker: “Fairchild card holder, then reputation.”

answers.answer: Setup deals 5 objective cards per player, and each courtship says to discard 1 objective card. The summary does not establish the normal number retained for scoring across the standard game, how simultaneous discards work, or whether tile objectives require upgraded tiles.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Deal 5 objective cards per player.” Courtship Round: “Discard 1 objective card.”

answers.answer: The summary says VP cards can be gained as benefits and that retained VP cards score at game end. It does not state when VP cards can be used for benefits or where used cards go.
answers.evidence: Standard Turn: favors may include “VP cards”; Scoring: “VP from retained VP cards.”

answers.answer: The summary says Black Rose tiles flip once when first used and hybrid (white flower) tiles flip each time used. It does not specify the flip rules for a normal activity tile, an already-upgraded tile, or a tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument. It also does not specify which hybrid category counts for courtship or objectives.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases: “Black rose tiles: Flip once when first used”; “Hybrid (white flower) tiles: Flip each time used; change category.”

answers.answer: The summary says Monuments provide reputation each turn at the start and that Servants’ Hall allows a gossip action that reduces an opponent’s reputation and gains yours. It does not distinguish hosting turns from pass turns, explain how gossip uses a servant, or say whether a player at minimum reputation can be targeted.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases: “Monuments: Provide reputation each turn at start”; “Servants’ Hall: Allows gossip action (reduce opponent reputation, gain yours).”

answers.answer: The summary does not mention Heritage Guest Suite, Queen’s Suite, or Lionheart Suite, so their guest use, service and doubling rules, subsequent tile state, and whether their single-guest count can change are unsupported.
answers.evidence: The summary contains no reference to these three suites.
